sections.html:
Hot Sulphur Springs is the county seat and Granby is the largest community. The county had 15,717 residents in 2020 and an estimate of 16,496 for 2025. Housing looks different from a typical suburb: 16,633 housing units against 7,006 households, with 57.9% of units vacant, which points to a lot of second homes. Of the occupied homes, 69.5% were owner-occupied and 30.5% rented.

Six towns sit inside the county: Fraser, Granby, Grand Lake, Hot Sulphur Springs, Kremmling and Winter Park. A parcel can be in a town, in an unincorporated area, or next to federal land such as Rocky Mountain National Park or Arapaho National Forest, and each setting has its own taxing districts. The Assessor keeps a tax area and tax authority list that sorts this out.

The Assessor values every property in the county. The Treasurer, who is also the Public Trustee, bills and collects. Both offices share a building in Hot Sulphur Springs.

OfficePhoneAddressHours
Assessor970-725-3060308 Byers Avenue, Hot Sulphur Springs; mail to P.O. Box 302Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.
Treasurer / Public Trustee970-725-3061308 Byers Avenue, Hot Sulphur Springs; mail to P.O. Box 288Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Both close on holidays. The Assessor's site also carries the mill levy certification, forms, comparable sales, a property record search and an online parcel map.

You can pay half in February and half in June, or send everything at once in April. Interest runs at 1% per month after each due date.

  • February 28: first half.
  • April 30: full payment.
  • June 15: second half.
  • July 1: delinquent notices go in the mail.
  • After September 1: cash or cashier's check only.
  • Usually November: the annual tax lien sale of delinquent taxes.

Notices are mailed once a year, normally in January. Whether or not one reaches you, paying on time is the owner's job. A returned check carries a $20 charge.

A Certificate of Taxes Due costs $10 in Grand County. Title companies ask for it before a sale closes, so a seller with a cash buyer should expect the request.

  • Certificate of Taxes Due: $10.00
  • Certificate of Authenticity for a mobile home: $10.00
  • Duplicate tax notice or receipt, current year: $2.00 each
  • Duplicate tax notice or receipt, prior year: $5.00 each
  • Research: $15.00 per hour, with the first hour paid when you ask

A mobile home is taxed apart from the land unless the title has been purged and the home sits permanently on a foundation. To transfer one, all taxes on it must be paid in full before the Treasurer issues the Certificate of Authenticity. The seller then takes that certificate and the signed title to the motor vehicle office.

The Assessor identifies, classifies and values all real and personal property in the county. Colorado revalues in odd-numbered years. In the years between, a Notice of Valuation goes only to owners whose value changed.

Call the Assessor at 970-725-3060 for the current protest deadline and the form to use, since the filing date is set each cycle and you will want it in writing.

A change in the residential assessment percentage is not grounds for a protest or an abatement of taxes. If the Assessor denies a protest or never answers, the next step is a written appeal to the County Board of Equalization.

The office that collects property tax also serves as Public Trustee, so a seller with a mortgage deals with one address in Hot Sulphur Springs. The Public Trustee handles information on releases of deeds of trust and on foreclosures.

When your loan is paid at closing, the lender asks for a release of the deed of trust, and that release clears the lien from the record. The county also posts Treasurer's deed notices, auction information and a tax liens page, which shows which parcels have unpaid taxes heading toward sale.

  • Phone for the Treasurer and Public Trustee: 970-725-3061.
  • Tax distribution reports and the mill levy certification (Form DLG 70) are posted on the county site.
  • The Assessor's FAQ explains how property taxes are determined, what a mill levy is and what an assessment rate is.

Many Grand County owners live elsewhere and get their mail there. Taxes are the owner's responsibility whether or not a bill arrives, so the address on file matters.

  • Update your address: the Treasurer has a mailing address change form, and the Assessor has a physical address change form.
  • Order a Certificate of Taxes Due before you list or accept an offer.
  • Confirm whether the home is in a town or an unincorporated area, because the tax area list can differ.
  • If a house has carried unpaid taxes since the prior year, delinquent taxes may be advertised and sold at the lien sale.

Back taxes do not stop a sale. Here is the usual sequence.

  1. The title company asks the Treasurer for the Certificate of Taxes Due.
  2. The certificate lists what is owed. Interest at 1% per month keeps adding to a late balance, so ask the Treasurer for a current figure at 970-725-3061 before closing.
  3. The balance is paid out of your proceeds when the sale closes.
  4. The lender or owner finishes the paperwork with the Public Trustee if a deed of trust needs to be released.

A cash buyer can still close with taxes owed. The balance and interest simply need to be confirmed with the Treasurer, so the number on the settlement statement is right.

Taxes touch a sale at four points, and the Treasurer's office is the stop for most of them.

  • Before listing: order the Certificate of Taxes Due, check whether the parcel is in a town or an unincorporated area, and make sure the mailing address on file is one you actually read.
  • When you accept an offer: hand the certificate to the title company so any balance and interest are known early.
  • At closing: unpaid taxes come out of your proceeds, and a loan payoff triggers the lender's request to release the deed of trust.
  • After closing: the buyer updates the mailing address, and you update yours for any final notices.

A cash sale cuts out showings, lender appraisals and repair negotiations. It does not cut out any of the tax steps above, so the Treasurer's phone number, 970-725-3061, is still the most useful one to have in hand.

faqs.q: When are Grand County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Half is due February 28 and half June 15, or the whole amount by April 30. Interest is 1% per month after each due date.

faqs.q: How do I find the Grand County appeal deadline?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor at 970-725-3060 for the current protest deadline, which is set each cycle. If a protest is denied, the next step is a written appeal to the County Board of Equalization.

faqs.q: How much is a Certificate of Taxes Due in Grand County?
Where is the Grand County Treasurer?
faqs.a: The office is at 308 Byers Avenue in Hot Sulphur Springs, open Monday to Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. The phone number is 970-725-3061.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Grand County house with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The taxes appear on the Certificate of Taxes Due and are normally settled at closing, including any interest. Delinquent taxes can also be sold at the lien sale, usually held in November.
